about: Two plugin-to-host requests, sent over the plugin's stdio like flow.run. The host announces ringPlan in plugin.init.features when it answers them; without it the plugin never offers transfer. oaiy.ring.plan asks who may be rung and for how long (the host's ring policy decides; the plugin enforces the answer). oaiy.ring.opened tells the host the request is open so it can start delivery (desktop toast, ring items); nothing waits for its answer. A host that does not answer the plan within 1.5 s, or answers something unusable, means nobody is rung: the tool result is unavailable with reason plan_unavailable.

init.about: The host announces ringPlan in the features of the plugin.init params when it answers oaiy.ring.plan and oaiy.ring.opened. Without it the plugin never offers the transfer tool. Every plugin.init replaces what the last one said, and a feature that merely resembles the name announces nothing. Transfer is offered on a call only when ringPlan is announced, at least one Companion device is approved in the private bootstrap roster, and consent currently grants both remote_assistance and remote_takeover (transfer-v1.start-ready.fixture.json).

plan.paramsRules: At most the last three caller turns, each cut to 300 characters; callerNumber is left out when unknown. The turns never leave the machine: the host runs the phrase checks on them.

results.plugin: For urgent and policy_rule the plugin skips its own phrase check (the caller asked for a person) only when the plan says reasonAllowed: true. A plan without it, or with anything but true, leaves the check in force: a ring for those reasons then needs the caller to have asked, and is otherwise refused (not_urgent for urgent, caller_did_not_ask for policy_rule) before anything is opened. caller_asked is unaffected: it is checked before the host is asked and no host word lifts it.

results.name: a desktop toast with no device named is not a target (design vector V01, fail closed)
results.plugin: Answers unavailable, reason no_endpoint, opens nothing and does not send oaiy.ring.opened, so no toast follows: a toast is a notification, not a target. A plan for the owner at the PC names the Windows Companion in desktopCompanions (see the next case).

results.plugin: Offers the request to that Windows Companion and to no other device, whether or not the Companion is running yet: it is offered the request when it connects inside the ring window.

targetRules.only: The plan names devices (phones and desktopCompanions, each once): the request is offered to those devices and no others, and no other device can accept it. On the relay carrier no other device can decline it either; on the socket carrier the plugin cannot attribute a decline to a key, so a device outside the plan can end the request with one (transfer-v1.md).
targetRules.nobody: The plan names no device, toast or not: nothing can be rung, and the answer is no_endpoint. A toast is not a target.

opened.paramsRules: expiresAt is Unix seconds: when the ring window ends. The host derives the reserved offer id of every phone in the plan from requestId and the phone's endpoint-key thumbprint (transfer-v1.reserved-offer-id.fixture.json), posts the ring items, and posts cancels when the request resolves.
